questions.question:
In the given figure, if AD = 3, DE = 4, AB = 12, BF = 2, FG = 6, BC = 10, then the value of frac M N is:

(Assume: M is the area of the quadrilateral FGDE and N is the area of the triangle ABC.)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87faef2bfffaf10eb6434dd8c11a0ae45ce02ad27bc586a43c8dafee68dfcc48.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87faef2bfffaf10eb6434dd8c11a0ae45ce02ad27bc586a43c8dafee68dfcc48.png] 

AD = 3, DE = 4, AB = 12, BF = 2, FG = 6, BC = 10

M is the area of the quadrilateral FGDE and N is the area of the triangle ABC.

**Formula used:**

Area of triangle = 1/2 × Multiple of adjacent sides × sin(Angle between those sides)

**Calculations:**

Area of ΔEBF = 1/2 × BE × BF × sinB

⇒ 1/2 × 5 × 2 × sinB (BE = AB - AD - DE)

⇒ 5 × sinB

Area of ΔDBG = 1/2 × BD × BG × sinB

⇒ 1/2 × 9 × 8 × sinB 

⇒ 36 × sinB

Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × BA × BC × sinB

⇒ 1/2 × 12 × 10 × sinB 

⇒ 60 × sinB

Area of quadrilateral FGDE(M) = Area of ΔDBG - Area of ΔEBF

⇒ 36sinB - 5sinB

⇒ 31sinB

Area of ΔABC(N) = 60sinB

⇒ M/N = (31sinB)/(60sinB)

⇒ 31/60

**∴ The value of (M/N) is 31/60.**

questions.question: ABC is a right - angled triangle, right angled at A in such a way that AB = AC and the bisector of angle B intersects the side AC at D. DM is perpendicular to BC, intersecting BC at M. If AB = 12 cm and BC = 12√2 cm, then find the length of side AD.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔABC, ∠A = 90° and AB = AC = 12 cm.

Angle bisector BD divides side AC in the ratio AD : DC = AB : BC.

Ratio AD : DC = 12 : 12√2 = 1 : √2.

Total ratio parts for AC = 1 + √2.

AD = [1 / (1 + √2)] × 12 = 12(√2 − 1) / (2 − 1) = 12(√2 − 1) cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12(√2 − 1) cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Triangle ABC is right-angled at A with AB = AC = 12 cm and BC = 12√2 cm. BD is the bisector of ∠B, and DM ⊥ BC.

**Formula Used:**

Angle Bisector Theorem: AD / DC = AB / BC

 
 
 
 A B C D M 12 cm 12√2 AD = 12(√2 − 1) cm 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since ∠A = 90° and AB = AC, triangle ABC is an isosceles right triangle.

⇒ In ΔABD and ΔMBD, ∠BAD = ∠BMD = 90°, BD is common, and ∠ABD = ∠MBD (BD is bisector).

⇒ ΔABD ≅ ΔMBD by AAS congruence, therefore AD = DM and AB = BM = 12 cm.

⇒ MC = BC − BM = 12√2 − 12 = 12(√2 − 1) cm.

⇒ In ΔDMC, ∠M = 90° and ∠C = 45° (as ∠A = 90°, AB = AC in ΔABC).

⇒ Therefore, ΔDMC is also an isosceles right triangle, which means DM = MC.

⇒ AD = DM = MC = 12(√2 − 1) cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12(√2 − 1) cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Theorem

In any triangle, the internal bisector of an angle divides the opposite side into segments whose lengths are in the same ratio as the other two sides. AD / DC = AB / BC.

Properties of Isosceles Right Triangle

A right-angled triangle with two equal legs has angles 90°, 45°, and 45°. The ratio of sides is always 1 : 1 : √2.

Congruency of Triangles

When two triangles are congruent (by SSS, SAS, ASA, or AAS), their corresponding parts (sides and angles) are exactly equal.
